excerpt: Previse is a London fintech that started with InstantPay for faster supplier payments and now turns B2B transaction data into AI insights for finance teams.
content:
Previse is a London financial technology company. It first became known for InstantPay, which TechCrunch described in 2020 as a way for large corporate buyers to pay suppliers quickly: machine learning looks at historical data to predict which invoices can safely be paid straight away and which are higher risk and need a manual check. At the time Previse said it processed about 100,000 invoices a day.

Its website now presents a broader data platform for finance teams. Previse connects to a company's ERP, accounts payable and receivable, source-to-pay, billing and CRM systems with no-code plugins, matches and monitors the data continuously, and turns it into analysis such as customer and supplier risk tracking, supply chain health checks, cash flow and liquidity management, fraud and error checks, and spend categorisation. Packaged products include SmartPay for automated early payments, SmartAccept for supplier enablement and SmartPlan for card programme forecasting, alongside consulting. It sells to enterprises, financial institutions and fintechs, and lists sites for the UK (covering EMEA and APAC) and the USA.

Paul Christensen founded Previse in 2016 and was its CEO when it raised money in 2020, according to TechCrunch.

Funding

Previse raised a $7 million Series A in 2018 led by Augmentum Fintech and Bessemer Venture Partners, UKTN reported. In April 2020 it raised $11 million led by Reefknot Investments and Mastercard, with Bessemer, Hambro Perks and Augmentum returning, taking total funding past $21.8 million, according to TechCrunch and Tech.eu.

Pricing

Previse does not publish prices. Its website asks companies to schedule a demo.

Who it suits

Previse suits finance, procurement and treasury teams at large companies, and banks or fintechs running supplier payment or card programmes, that want insight from transaction data spread across several systems. Small businesses are not its target.

We have not tested Previse. This page is based on its website (checked 15 October 2026) and on TechCrunch, Tech.eu and UKTN.
